key_insight: The paper shows that fairness in medical imaging can be improved by optimizing across hidden appearance-based patient cohorts rather than only visible demographic groups.
clinical_relevance: This could help reduce model performance gaps across patients, including cases where multiple demographic attributes create sparse subgroup data and harder-to-detect inequities.
method: Cluster images into K latent cohorts using image appearance.
Apply fairness optimization across these hidden cohorts instead of demographic labels.
Test whether this also reduces disparities across single and multiple demographic attributes.
evidence_signal: On the proposed HIDFairBench benchmark, the approach is reported to achieve state-of-the-art fairness results on both single and multiple demographic attributes without using demographic labels for training.
watch_item: Appearance-based clusters may not map cleanly to clinically meaningful subgroups, so cohort interpretability and validation are important before deployment.
paper_title: Fairness Beyond Demographics: Optimizing Performance Across Appearance-Based Hidden Cohorts in Medical Imaging
